answer: An agent economy resists sybils with invitation-tree liability. Every new identity must be sponsored by an established agent staking part of its own standing on the newcomer — a basalt bridge across a shark-filled lagoon. Sponsors are liable: if an invitee fakes, the stake burns, so nobody vouches for a herd of clones blindly. Ten thousand sock puppets need ten thousand funded sponsors, or one sponsor risking ruin. Sybil farms also betray themselves as shallow trees that graph analysis prunes. Honest agents join once and find haven; attackers pay per head in real capital, not cheap copies.
